reformulation: Exact cleanup plus binary-conflict disaggregation of a 1,166-var / 2,295-row MIP (738 integers, minimize x1, optimum unchanged at 12890): delete 120 continuous variables forced to 0 by a singleton UP row (60 in x6..x124, 60 in x125..x243) and their terms, fold 118 retained singleton upper bounds into BOUNDS, remove 588 box-implied rows (587 singletons + the empty c1839) and 74 exact duplicates with retained witnesses, replace the 75 rows z+(1/4)sum(y)<=1 of degree <=4 by their 246 implied pair conflicts qedge1..qedge246, and keep the 13 larger aggregates (c1255 c1256 c1257 c1258 c1259 c1260 c1264 c1265 c1311 c1313 c1400 c1482 c1484). Target 1,046 vars / 1,804 rows / 27,310 nonzeros.
claim_class: 3 directional claims: (0) forward integer affine bijection source->target, (1) reverse integer bijection target->source, (2) reverse with integrality dropped, i.e. target LP contained in source LP; all three objective Equal over the same 1,046-coordinate projection, inverse indices 1/0/None. No strictness, no point witness, no solver claim.
claims: 3 claims / 3 blocks, one block per claim (tools/prepare_test14.py:65,70). counts.obligations_by_claim = [6845, 7456, 5672] - claim 0 (forward, integers kept) 6845, claim 1 (reverse, integers kept) 7456, claim 2 (reverse, LP only) 5672; each block ends in Return{map:[1046 forward / 1166 reverse affine expressions], checks:[one ref or the literal 'Exact' per obligation]}.

Obligation order per claim: VarLower/VarUpper for every output variable (plus VarInt when integrality is kept), one check per output row, an Eq for the objective difference, then a literal 'Exact' for every projection coordinate, and the full inverse composition on the opposite coordinate list (claim 0 inverse=1, claim 1 inverse=0, claim 2 inverse=None).

The reverse claims re-derive all 2,295 source rows: a retained row is referenced directly when it survives, otherwise it is substituted through the 120 proved zero facts (122 retained rows carry deleted zero terms, tools/prepare_test14.py:56); a removed row routes by audit reason - box activity (588), duplicate witness identity (74), or a 1/4-weighted sum of the added conflict rows plus the center upper bound weight 1-n/4 (75 small aggregates, tools/prepare_test14.py:51).

The forward claim proves every original aggregate row and each of the 246 added conflicts by a binary Cases split on the center (kernel statistics branches=246): branch center=1 is VarUpper(j)+assumption, branch center=0 is 4*aggregate + neighbor VarLower terms + 3*assumption (tools/prepare_test14.py:26-27).

The exploratory covering-domination certificates (266 proved, 5 inconclusive: c2140 c2156 c2158 c2279 c2294) are deliberately not asserted: no covering row was deleted by domination, only 73 as exact duplicates (cases/test14/README.md; digest audit.json hypotheses.covering_rows_removed_as_exact_duplicates).
proof_encoding: RPA 2 text = 'RPA 2\n' + one compact JSON object with keys {'claims':[3 claim specs],'blocks':[3 blocks]} (tools/prepare_test14.py:70); request.json 31,829 B holds the same 3 claim specs, each carrying its own 1,046-pair projection list.

Step kinds used: Lin (linear_terms 6,904), EqPair (the 120 zero fixings), Cases (246 binary splits, each with two Witness branches); no lifts, no points, no bijections (cases/test14/preparation.json kernel_runs[3] statistics).

Refs: {'Local':id} into the per-block fact table, row refs {'RowUpper'|'RowLower'|'RowEq':i}, atoms {'VarLower'|'VarUpper'|'VarInt':i}, and {'Assumption':k}; trivial obligations are emitted as the bare string 'Exact' and a single-term fact collapses to the premise ref itself (tools/prepare_test54.py:16-24).

Receipts: proof.rpa 640,705 B -> proof.rpx 409,517 B (sha256 b341ac27de11af6dc808aad71784d672cf33e56c17f131ee8b94df6d4549daa3); source.mcm 675,243 B, target.mcm 613,130 B; obligations 19,973, work 434,761, substitution_terms 87,457, peak_live_facts 608, execute 20,030 us, total 27,668 us; preparation 0.836 s (cases/test14/preparation.json).

Budgets are not near binding in this case: work 434,761 against 1e9, RPX 0.4 MB against 256 MiB, 246 branches against depth 64 (the smallest RPA in the corpus still carries 19,973 obligations), so the cost of this case lies entirely in generating the certificate, not in verifying it.
agent_manual_work: Parsed the 1,027,159-B MPS with two independent decoders (whitespace-token and fixed-field slices) and cross-checked every row, coefficient, RHS record, bound record and INTORG/INTEND marker; verify.py then contained a third fixed-field reader for the generated artifact (output/verify.py:11).

Ran the structural sweeps by hand: complete singleton inspection (120 zeros, 118 foldable upper bounds, 587 singleton rows, 1 empty row), exhaustive positively-scaled duplicate scan (202 groups, 203 excess rows), 271 covering-row supports matched against 238 demand rows, 88 quarter rows -> 246 pairs vs 136 existing unit packing edges, incidence traversal (1 component over 1,166 variables).

Wrote the target model as fixed-column MPS text by hand - exact decimal encoder asserted through Decimal prec 50, two-pairs-per-line packing, INTORG/INTEND re-emission - plus a 274,619-B audit.json, and re-serialized the whole file after retracting the 13 unweighted capacity rows.

Wrote and ran an 11,256-B / 216-line independent verifier (output/verify.py) that re-derived 737 removal proofs, 4,344 binary truth-table assignments and 266 covering certificates and checked SHA-256 hashes; 4 runs with 3 patches, one of them caused by its own wrong assumption about covering rows.

friction: Every precondition of the five rule patterns is a generator-side assert (tools/prepare_test14.py:16,20,26,49,51): a violated premise is a Python traceback, and the notion of an obligation family (588 box rows, 246 splits, 120 fixings, 122 zero-term substitutions) exists only in the Python code, never as a kernel-visible object.

The generator re-materialises every fact to compare expressions (assert p.refexpr(check)==wanted at :37, :49, :56) and accumulates 87,457 substitution terms and 6,904 linear terms in Python dictionaries; SparseBuilder exists only because the naive Builder copies fact maps (tools/prepare_test70.py:14-16), and cases_le is duplicated in prepare_test19.py:13, prepare_test70.py:32 and prepare_test70_subset_global.py:32.

The certificate is keyed on the agent's audit.json schema: h['binary_implication_changes'] rows carry center/neighbors/edge_rows/retained_aggregate_row and h['removed_rows'][rn]['reason'] decides which obligation is emitted, while degree>4 vs <=4 is only 'assert n<=4' (:51) - a renamed key or a re-derived edge list silently changes the proof.

The same 1,046-pair projection list is materialised in all three claims (request.json 31,829 B) and the same remaining-coordinate map is the Return.map of blocks 0 and 1 (1,046 expressions against 1,166 in block 1's inverse list), because a block cannot reference another block's facts.

Mutation testing is positional surgery on the emitted JSON (tools/prepare_test14.py:81-85): a mutation cannot name the claim/step/term it attacks, and 3 of the 4 rejects report only 'INVALID obligation mismatch: expected Le' (one adds 'obligation 3590'; none names a claim, block or step).
